summary_en: The enalapril label names spironolactone as a medicine that can raise blood potassium a lot when taken with enalapril, so potassium should be checked often.
reviewer_comment: Vasotec label (enalapril) names spironolactone as an example of a potassium-sparing diuretic that can markedly raise serum potassium. Basis corrected from class to pair-specific.
evidence_section: Vasotec label, Drug Interactions: Agents Increasing Serum Potassium (names spironolactone); also Aldactone 7.1 lists ACE inhibitors: https://api.fda.gov/drug/label.json?search=openfda.generic_name:%22spironolactone%22+AND+openfda.brand_name:%22aldactone%22&limit=1
evidence_note: Enalapril label names spironolactone as raising potassium; spironolactone label lists ACE inhibitors the same way.

summary_en: The ramipril label names spironolactone as a medicine that raises the risk of high blood potassium, and asks for frequent potassium checks.
reviewer_comment: Ramipril label 7.1 names spironolactone; summary faithful.
evidence_section: Ramipril capsules label, 7.1 Diuretics (names spironolactone); also Aldactone 7.1: https://api.fda.gov/drug/label.json?search=openfda.generic_name:%22spironolactone%22+AND+openfda.brand_name:%22aldactone%22&limit=1
evidence_note: Ramipril label names spironolactone as raising hyperkalemia risk; asks for frequent potassium checks.

summary_en: The olmesartan label names spironolactone as a medicine that can raise blood potassium and advises checking potassium.
reviewer_comment: Benicar label 7.1 names spironolactone; summary faithful.
evidence_section: Benicar label, 7.1 Agents Increasing Serum Potassium (names spironolactone); also Aldactone 7.1: https://api.fda.gov/drug/label.json?search=openfda.generic_name:%22spironolactone%22+AND+openfda.brand_name:%22aldactone%22&limit=1
evidence_note: Olmesartan label names spironolactone among potassium-raising agents and advises monitoring potassium.

summary_en: The losartan label warns that other medicines which raise potassium can cause high blood potassium, and the spironolactone label lists ARBs such as losartan among them.
reviewer_comment: Cozaar 7.1 warns about other drugs that raise serum potassium without naming spironolactone. Class membership: the COZAAR label (Indications) calls losartan an angiotensin II receptor blocker (ARB); the Aldactone label 7.1 lists ARBs as drugs that can raise potassium. The Vasotec label names spironolactone as a potassium-raising diuretic.
evidence_section: Cozaar label, 7.1 Agents Increasing Serum Potassium; Cozaar 1 Indications (ARB); Aldactone 7.1: https://api.fda.gov/drug/label.json?search=openfda.generic_name:%22spironolactone%22+AND+openfda.brand_name:%22aldactone%22&limit=1
evidence_note: Losartan label warns of high potassium with other potassium-raising drugs; spironolactone label lists ARBs as such drugs.

summary_en: The telmisartan label warns that potassium-sparing diuretics can cause high blood potassium in people taking telmisartan, and spironolactone is one of them.
reviewer_comment: CORRECTION: the recorded Micardis search URL now returns the Micardis HCT combination label. Verified instead on the single-ingredient telmisartan tablets label (Amneal, set id 20a60231...): 5.3 Hyperkalemia names potassium-sparing diuretics and other potassium-raising drugs for ARB users; Indications calls telmisartan an ARB. Spironolactone is named as a potassium-sparing diuretic in the Vasotec and ramipril labels.
evidence_section: Telmisartan tablets label (FDA), 5.3 Hyperkalemia and 1 Indications (ARB); Aldactone 7.1: https://api.fda.gov/drug/label.json?search=openfda.generic_name:%22spironolactone%22+AND+openfda.brand_name:%22aldactone%22&limit=1
evidence_note: Telmisartan label warns of high potassium with potassium-sparing diuretics; spironolactone is such a diuretic.

summary_en: The ramipril label says that using telmisartan and ramipril together is not recommended: in a large trial the combination gave no extra benefit and more kidney problems.
reviewer_comment: Ramipril label 5.7 names telmisartan (ONTARGET) and says use together is not recommended. Old summary also mentioned potassium and blood pressure, which 5.7 does not say; rewritten. Severity left unclassified.
evidence_section: Ramipril capsules label, 5.7 Dual Blockade of the Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System (names telmisartan)
evidence_note: Ramipril label: telmisartan plus ramipril gave no extra benefit and more kidney problems in a trial; combination not recommended.

summary_en: The losartan label says that combining an ARB with an ACE inhibitor raises the chance of low blood pressure, fainting, high potassium and kidney changes, and a trial showed no added benefit; ramipril is an ACE inhibitor.
reviewer_comment: Cozaar 7.4 covers ARB plus ACE inhibitor generally. Ramipril is an ACE inhibitor per its own label ("ACE inhibitor use has been associated with..."); losartan is an ARB per Cozaar Indications. Summary rewritten because the Cozaar text does not itself say "avoid".
evidence_section: Cozaar label, 7.4 Dual Blockade of the Renin-Angiotensin System; Cozaar 1 Indications (ARB); Ramipril label 5 (ACE inhibitor): https://api.fda.gov/drug/label.json?search=openfda.generic_name:ramipril&limit=1
evidence_note: Losartan label: ARB plus ACE inhibitor raises risks of low pressure, fainting, high potassium and kidney change; ramipril is an ACE inhibitor.

summary_en: The enalapril label says combining an ACE inhibitor with an ARB raises the chance of low blood pressure, high potassium and kidney changes and that such combinations should generally be avoided; losartan is an ARB.
reviewer_comment: Vasotec label states dual RAS blockade with ARBs, ACE inhibitors or aliskiren raises risks and says to avoid combined use in general. Losartan is an ARB per Cozaar Indications; enalapril is an ACE inhibitor per its own label.
evidence_section: Vasotec label, Precautions: Dual Blockade of the Renin-Angiotensin System; Cozaar 1 Indications (ARB): https://api.fda.gov/drug/label.json?search=openfda.generic_name:%22losartan+potassium%22+AND+openfda.brand_name:%22cozaar%22&limit=1
evidence_note: Enalapril label: ARB plus ACE inhibitor raises low-pressure, potassium and kidney risks; avoid combined use in general.

summary_en: The levofloxacin label says blood sugar can become too low or too high in people also taking a diabetes medicine, so it should be monitored closely; gliclazide is a diabetes tablet.
reviewer_comment: Levofloxacin 7.3 refers to any antidiabetic agent. Gliclazide is an oral blood-glucose-lowering drug (NHS gliclazide page; WHO ATC A10BB09, sulfonylureas). Old summary cited a glyburide example that 7.3 does not contain; rewritten. Severity left unclassified.
evidence_section: Levofloxacin tablets label, 7.3 Antidiabetic Agents; WHO ATC index A10BB09 gliclazide (Sulfonylureas): https://atcddd.fhi.no/atc_ddd_index/?code=A10BB09&showdescription=no
evidence_note: Levofloxacin label: blood sugar can go too low or too high with an antidiabetic agent; gliclazide is a diabetes tablet.

summary_en: The ciprofloxacin label warns of low blood sugar, sometimes severe, when it is taken with diabetes tablets (mainly sulfonylureas); gliclazide is a sulfonylurea.
reviewer_comment: Ciprofloxacin Table 11 names oral antidiabetic drugs, mainly sulfonylureas, for low blood sugar (sometimes severe). WHO ATC places gliclazide in A10BB sulfonylureas. Severity left unclassified.
evidence_section: Ciprofloxacin tablets label, 7 Drug Interactions (oral antidiabetic drugs, mainly sulfonylureas); 5.19 Blood Glucose Disturbances; WHO ATC index A10BB09: https://atcddd.fhi.no/atc_ddd_index/?code=A10BB09&showdescription=no
evidence_note: Ciprofloxacin label: low blood sugar, sometimes severe, with oral antidiabetic drugs mainly sulfonylureas; gliclazide is a sulfonylurea.

summary_en: The domperidone product information says it must not be taken with medicines that lengthen the heart's QT interval and names levofloxacin among such antibiotics.
reviewer_comment: Verified against current product information, not only the 2014 annex: HPRA (Irish regulator) Motilium 10 mg leaflet (revised Sept 2022) tells people not to take it with levofloxacin among named antibiotics; the HPRA SmPC and EMA Annex III list levofloxacin under contraindicated QTc-prolonging medicines (4.3/4.5). The current UK SmPC (revised 04/11/2025, read on emc.medicines.org.uk, not a regulator domain) has the same wording. The source states contraindicated, so severity major.
evidence_section: HPRA Motilium 10 mg film-coated tablets leaflet, section 2 (do not take with ... levofloxacin); EMA Annex III SmPC 4.3/4.5: https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/referral/domperidone-article-31-referral-annex-iii_en.pdf
evidence_note: Domperidone product information names levofloxacin among QT-prolonging antibiotics that must not be used together with it.

summary_en: The domperidone product information asks for caution with azithromycin because both can affect the heart's QT interval.
reviewer_comment: Domperidone SmPC 4.5 says caution with the macrolides azithromycin and roxithromycin (QT). HPRA SmPC (2015) and EMA Annex III agree; the current UK SmPC (rev. 04/11/2025, via emc) has the same wording. Caution, not contraindication, so severity stays unclassified.
evidence_section: HPRA domperidone SmPC, 4.5 (caution: azithromycin and roxithromycin); EMA Annex III 4.5: https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/referral/domperidone-article-31-referral-annex-iii_en.pdf ; Azithromycin label 5.4 QT Prolongation: https://api.fda.gov/drug/label.json?search=openfda.generic_name:azithromycin&limit=1
evidence_note: Domperidone SmPC asks for caution with azithromycin because both can lengthen QT; azithromycin label confirms QT risk.

summary_en: Domperidone is not to be used with medicines that lengthen the heart's QT interval, and the ondansetron label says ondansetron can do this.
reviewer_comment: Domperidone SmPC 4.3/4.5 contraindicates QT-prolonging medicines as a class (list "representative and not exhaustive"); ondansetron is not named. The ondansetron FDA label 5.2 states QT prolongation. Severity kept unclassified because the pair itself is not named.
evidence_section: HPRA domperidone SmPC 4.3/4.5 (QT-prolonging drugs); EMA Annex III: https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/referral/domperidone-article-31-referral-annex-iii_en.pdf ; Ondansetron tablets label 5.2 QT Prolongation: https://api.fda.gov/drug/label.json?search=openfda.generic_name:ondansetron&limit=1
evidence_note: Domperidone is not to be used with QT-prolonging medicines; the ondansetron label says ondansetron lengthens QT.

summary_en: Domperidone is not to be used with medicines that lengthen the heart's QT interval, and the ciprofloxacin label says ciprofloxacin can do this.
reviewer_comment: Same class reasoning as S13. Ciprofloxacin label states QT prolongation and torsade de pointes reports (Highlights; 5.12). Severity kept unclassified.
evidence_section: HPRA domperidone SmPC 4.3/4.5 (QT-prolonging drugs); EMA Annex III: https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/referral/domperidone-article-31-referral-annex-iii_en.pdf ; Ciprofloxacin tablets label 5.12 QT Prolongation: https://api.fda.gov/drug/label.json?search=openfda.generic_name:ciprofloxacin+AND+openfda.route:ORAL&limit=1
evidence_note: Domperidone is not to be used with QT-prolonging medicines; the ciprofloxacin label says ciprofloxacin lengthens QT.

summary_en: The vildagliptin product information says taking it with an ACE inhibitor may raise the chance of angioedema (swelling of the face, lips or throat); enalapril is an ACE inhibitor.
reviewer_comment: Galvus SmPC 4.5 "Combination with ACE-inhibitors: there may be an increased risk of angioedema". Enalapril is an ACE inhibitor per its own label. Severity unclassified.
evidence_section: Galvus SmPC (EMA), 4.5 Combination with ACE-inhibitors; 4.8; Vasotec label (enalapril is an ACE inhibitor): https://api.fda.gov/drug/label.json?search=openfda.generic_name:%22enalapril+maleate%22+AND+openfda.brand_name:%22vasotec%22&limit=1
evidence_note: Vildagliptin SmPC: possible higher angioedema risk with ACE inhibitors; enalapril is an ACE inhibitor.

summary_en: The vildagliptin product information says taking it with an ACE inhibitor may raise the chance of angioedema (swelling of the face, lips or throat); ramipril is an ACE inhibitor.
reviewer_comment: As S15; ramipril is an ACE inhibitor per its own label.
evidence_section: Galvus SmPC (EMA), 4.5 Combination with ACE-inhibitors; 4.8; Ramipril label (ACE inhibitor): https://api.fda.gov/drug/label.json?search=openfda.generic_name:ramipril&limit=1
evidence_note: Vildagliptin SmPC: possible higher angioedema risk with ACE inhibitors; ramipril is an ACE inhibitor.
